$comment: Size and performance budgets, defined once. Byte limits are binary (1 KiB = 1024 B). scope says who enforces each one: dist = scripts/check-dist.mjs after every build; repo and e2e = the repository and browser tests, which are not in this repository yet (until then those budgets are targets, checked by hand).

publicFileBytes.what: any single non-HTML file in dist/: everything copied from public/, and _astro/ files (the largest is a hero loop, which the media script keeps under 1 MiB)

tileLoopBytes.what: each tile or figure loop, media/<name>-<w>.mp4|webm: max for w <= 640, maxHiDpi for the wider rendition served to high-density screens (the limits the media script encodes to)

heroLoopBytes.what: each project hero loop: media/<name>-hero-<w>.mp4|webm, or any loop rendered 1280 px wide or wider (the limit the media script encodes to)

htmlBytes.what: each HTML page, including its inlined CSS (and so the inlined font)

inlineCssBytes.what: the contents of every <style> element on one page, including the font, which is inlined as a data: URI (about 21 KiB)

inlineJsBytes.what: the contents of every inline <script> on one page (JSON data blocks excluded)

externalJsBytes.what: all _astro/*.js files together (the diagram script; limit = measured x 1.5)

firstLoadBytes.what: bytes transferred for one page before any scrolling

fontRequests.what: font files requested by one page (the font is inlined into the CSS, so none)

cls.what: cumulative layout shift of one page, at every tested width and on throttled slow 4G; must stay below max (sub-pixel shifts of a few 1e-5 occur)

lcpSlow4gMs.what: largest contentful paint in ms under slow-4G throttling
